prompt: ugh ok I need help thinking something through. I'm supposed to send my director a note about our team's shared drive situation. Things I'm thinking: the drive is a mess, nobody can find anything, we had a near miss last week where someone almost sent an outdated version of the readiness slides to the wing commander, IT says they're migrating everyone to SharePoint sometime next year anyway, two people on the team already started their own folder systems, I spent like 3 hours last week hunting for a file, and honestly I'd be willing to own a cleanup but I don't want to sign up for a huge project. I don't even know what I'm actually asking for. Can you help me figure out what my point is before I write anything?
assertions: The response does not jump straight to a finished note/email draft; it works toward the user's main point first
The response identifies the reader (the director) and what the reader needs to decide or do
The response offers a tentative governing thought stated as a single assertion or ask, and invites the user to confirm or correct it
The response groups the user's thoughts by kind and treats the user's willingness/reluctance to own the cleanup as separate from the reasons supporting the point
The response asks no more than 4 questions of the user
